July 10, 1972
32
The Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
U. S. Department of the Interior
Washington, D. C.
Re: Draft of Environmental Statement
Proposed Departmental Implementation of Executive Order
11644 Pertaining to the Use of Off-Road Vehicles on the
Public Lands
Gentlemen:
Please consider the following statement in connection with the above draft:
Since Executive Order 11644 was issued in February, 1972, there has been no interpretation of its effect on the use of off-road vehicles in the exploration for minerals, including oil, non-metallics, and metallics. Of particular interest is the possible effect on the use of the equipment essential for subsurface exploration. In general, this equipment is carried on off-road vehicles, and a proper field procedure usually requires use on a regular grid pattern, which is, of course, compatible only with off-road use.
The intent of Executive Order 11644 appears to be to limit indiscriminate use of off-road vehicles, but it is so broad that it may apply to off-road use of vehicles in connection with the exploration for mineral deposits. This possible application would be contrary to the requirements of the mining law that the public lands shall be open for mineral exploration and location.
The Departmental implementation of the Executive Order should specifically not include the use of off-road vehicles used in connection with the exploration for mineral deposits.
On page 10, lines 5 and 6 up from the bottom, say: "Public participation will be solicited on each area prior to its designation as open (with controls) or closed to ORV use." Attempts to participate in all such areas of interest will be extremely time consuming, expensive, and burdensome to people in the mining industry.
